---
title: "Shared and Mutable References"
---

# Shared and Mutable References
Instead of transferring ownership, a function can access data via **references**. This mechanism is called **borrowing**.

### Shared References (`&T`)

Shared references allow read-only access to data without taking ownership:

```rust
fn calculate_length(s: &String) -> usize {
    s.len()
}

fn main() {
    let s = String::from("desk");
    let len = calculate_length(&s); // Pass reference
    println!("The length of '{}' is {}.", s, len); // s is still valid!
}
```

### Mutable References (`&mut T`)

Mutable references permit modifying the borrowed value:

```rust
fn append_status(s: &mut String) {
    s.push_str(" [ACTIVE]");
}

fn main() {
    let mut task = String::from("Process orders");
    append_status(&mut task);
    println!("{}", task);
}
```
